results.title: 70% Local gold refining by 2027 : CLGB highlights key enablers
results.content: The Chamber of Licensed Gold Buyers (CLGB) has underscored the importance of strategic investment in infrastructure, financing and sector formalisation to support Ghana’s ambition of refining 70 per cent of artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold locally by December 2027. In its policy position on the 2027 Budget, the Chamber welcomed the Government’s strategic direction to transition Ghana from the export of raw minerals towards greater domestic refining, value addition and industrial development. CLGB considers this ambition a significant opportunity to deepen local participation in the gold value chain, strengthen national economic resilience and maximise the developmental benefits of the country’s mineral resources. results.title: Housing Minister pushes development bank to unlock housing finance
results.content: Ghana needs a dedicated development bank to provide affordable long-term financing for housing developers and support the delivery of affordable homes, Ahmed Ibrahim, Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources, has said.

results.title: Government to construct Inland Fisheries Market in Accra in 2027 – Emelia Arthur
results.content: The Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture, Emelia Arthur, has announced plans to construct an Inland Fisheries Market in Accra next year, using funds allocated to the Ministry in the 2027 Budget.

results.title: 51% of young voters satisfied with 24-hour economy policy – Global InfoAnalytics poll
results.content: More than half of young voters in Ghana have expressed satisfaction with the government’s 24-hour Economy policy, although the initiative has received weaker approval than three other youth-focused programmes, a Global InfoAnalytics poll has found.

results.title: Illegal mining, destructive fishing threaten inland fisheries – Vice President
results.content: Vice-President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for urgent action to protect Ghana's inland fisheries, warning that illegal mining, destructive fishing practices and climate change are placing increasing pressure on the country's aquatic resources and the livelihoods they support.

results.title: Payroll without pipettes: Why you cannot build a first-world economy on 0.09% R&D
results.content: Read Section 3 of the 2027 Budget Statement and the ambition leaps off the page. Government promises a "New Economy" built on critical-minerals refining, biomanufacturing, nuclear baseload power, and a National Artificial Intelligence Centre.
